topIssues.title: Proofs: Increase `MAX_CLOCK_DURATION` and reduce air gap constants (keeping 7 day total) in preparation for faster withdrawals with ZK
topIssues.author: pauldowman
topIssues.body:
The finality delay and the proof maturity delay are both constants, and the contract implementation is shared. So we can't reduce them for ZK and 1-day withdrawals if there are still other chains using fault proofs, since stage 1 requires 7 days in total. For example if `DISPUTE_GAME_FINALITY_DELAY_SECONDS` becomes 12 hours to provide fast withdrawals on ZK dispute games, then it would reduce FaultDisputeGame to 4 days total. 

To be configurable per-chain they would need to become constructor args. But aside from this transition period from fault proofs to ZK proofs, they don't really need to be configurable per chain.

Instead, we can reduce the finality delay (for all chains) to e.g. 12 hours, and increase `MAX_CLOCK_DURATION` to 6.5 days.

topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: own the log layer — op-service/log becomes the monorepo logging API
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #21745 (§15 of the [op-geth decoupling doc](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1657fbe391d3f37785a6a3609422ee79fe86d9fa/docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md#L416-L436)). **Blocks #20266.**

`op-service/log` becomes the monorepo's logging API: no monorepo Go file imports `go-ethereum/log`. This is better layering regardless of the decoupling — the fork's `Logger.SetContext`/`WriteCtx`/`LogAttrs`/`Trace…ErrorContext` extensions are just what forces it.

## Scope (measured at 1657fbe)

- **697** monorepo Go files import `github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/log` — op-node 121, op-service 82, op-challenger 71, op-e2e 65, op-dispute-mon 48, op-test-sequencer 42, op-devstack 37, op-chain-ops 36, op-deployer 33, op-supernode 27, op-batcher 21, op-conductor 20, and a long tail. (`superchain-registry/` is a submodule with its own Go module — out of scope, flagged to that team.)
- **63** of those import *both* `geth/log` and `oplog`, so they need symbol-level dedup, not a blind import rewrite.
- Only ~13 files use the fork's context extensions at all: [`op-service/testlog`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1657fbe391d3f37785a6a3609422ee79fe86d9fa/op-service/testlog/testlog.go), [`op-service/log/logfilter`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/tree/1657fbe391d3f37785a6a3609422ee79fe86d9fa/op-service/log/logfilter), `op-service/tls/tlsinfo.go`, `op-devstack/devtest`, plus a handful of call sites. Phase 2 is therefore small; phase 1 is the bulk.

## PRs

1. **`op-service/log`: add the `oplog` logger surface.** `type Logger = log.Logger` (alias) plus re-exports of the package-level API actually in use: `New`, `NewLogger`, `Root`, `SetDefault`, `With`, `Info/Warn/Error/Debug/Trace/Crit`, the `Level*`/`Lvl*` constants, `LevelFromString`, `FromLegacyLevel`, `DiscardHandler`, `NewTerminalHandler[WithLevel]`, `JSONHandler`, `LogfmtHandlerWithLevel`, `Handler`. Migrate `op-service` itself as the first consumer.
2. **Tree-wide sweep + gate.** Rewrite the remaining ~615 files to `oplog`, dedup the 63 dual-import files, and add a lint/CI gate (golangci `depguard`, or a grep check) that fails any new `go-ethereum/log` import. Pure rename while the alias holds — zero behaviour change; build + test is the gate. Land fast to avoid rebase churn against everything in flight.
3. **Flip the alias to an owned interface** *(at cutover)*. Replace the alias with an interface — upstream's method set plus the context methods — over an `slog`-backed implementation. Do **not** copy upstream's LGPL `log` package; the context-extension logic is OP-authored and ports over. Our interface is a superset of upstream's, so an `oplog.Logger` still satisfies `log.Logger` wherever we hand one into geth code (e.g. the in-process L1 geth in op-e2e).

PRs 1–2 land now and are independent of the rest of the epic. PR 3 lands with or just before the go.mod flip.

## Acceptance criteria

- No monorepo Go file imports `go-ethereum/log`, enforced by a CI/lint gate.
- `op-service/log/logfilter` and `op-service/testlog` build on the owned API with unchanged behaviour.
- After PR 3, `op-service/log` has no `go-ethereum/log` dependency, and an `oplog.Logger` is still accepted by geth APIs taking `log.Logger`.

topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
Lagoon currently requires separate tools and pre-funded senders to exercise Interop and SDM together. `check-lagoon all` now takes one funded account, deterministically derives and tops up a separate SDM sender on both chains, then concurrently runs the complete Interop smoke suite and policy-producing SDM workloads on both chains; focused `sdm` subcommands remain available for generated or existing-block checks. Legacy nonzero PostExec `gasPrice` responses remain compatible, and `sdm-devnet` remains temporarily for existing Kupcake wrappers.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22988

topPRs.title: kona-sp1-proposer: recover refund-mode bonds
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Recovers proposer bonds when a ZK dispute game closes in `REFUND` distribution mode. The proposer discovers historical refundable games, carries their complete resolution dependency chain forward, and completes both phases of the `DelayedWETH` withdrawal without making those games eligible for new creation or proving work.

This is the second PR in a two-PR stack and is based on #22787.

## Stack

1. #22787 — ancestry eligibility
2. #22835 — refund-mode bond recovery (this PR)

Review #22787 first. With its branch selected as this PR's base, this diff contains only refund lifecycle behavior.

## High-level changes

- Add dispute-game bond distribution mode and refund-credit reads to the proposer adapter boundary.
- Classify claimable credit by mode: normal `credit` for legacy distribution and `refundModeCredit` for `REFUND`.
- Retain proposer-created blacklisted, retired, or terminally invalid games only while needed to finish resolution or recover bonds.
- Retain and permissionlessly resolve foreign or unknown-prestate ancestors required to advance a proposer refund, including cold-history discovery where canonical super-root data is unavailable.
- Keep blacklist and retirement quarantine reversible so a later registered anchor can rehabilitate inherited descendants.
- Drive the two-step `DelayedWETH` lifecycle: unlock credit first, then claim the matured withdrawal.
- Discover refundable games on cold start or factory reset across the complete factory history, including entries older than the deadline cutoff or before an unsupported-type anchor.
- Keep incremental-scan cutoffs while advancing the cursor only after a complete successful walk.
- Pin lifecycle and standing reads to the synchronization block so mode, status, and claim decisions use one L1 view.

## Review guide

1. `contract.rs`: generated bindings for distribution mode and refund credit.
2. `ports.rs` and `adapters.rs`: mode-aware bond state and pinned reads.
3. `proposer.rs` discovery: cold-history refund and dependency recovery versus incremental cutoffs.
4. `proposer.rs` lifecycle classification: dependency resolution, retention, unlock, and payout decisions.
5. Unit and scenario tests: blacklisted refunds, foreign dependency chains, reversible quarantine, two-phase claims, and startup recovery.

## Verification

- `cargo nextest run -p kona-sp1-proposer` — 236 passed.
- `mise exec -- just lint` — passed; only pre-existing Cargo manifest deprecation warnings were emitted.

topPRs.title: op-service/log: own the Logger and its slog implementation
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
`op-service/log` now owns its `Logger`: an immutable interface with upstream go-ethereum's method set, minus `Write`, plus `WithContext`, `LogAttrs` and the `*Context` methods. It is backed by our own slog implementation. `op-service/log`, `logfilter` and `testlog` compile and pass their tests against upstream go-ethereum with the `replace` dropped. Before this, they depended on op-geth's logger methods and would break at the cutover.

Output is byte-identical to geth's logger for the terminal, logfmt and JSON handlers, which a differential test pins. Level filtering, the `!BADKEY` handling of an odd argument and `Crit` exiting match op-geth. Two things change on purpose, both to simplify:
- op-geth's mutable `SetContext` is replaced by `WithContext(ctx) Logger`, which returns a derived logger. Every call site already derived a fresh logger and then set its context, so each becomes one call.
- Every method attributes records to its direct caller. `Write`/`WriteCtx` no longer attribute to the caller's caller, and they are gone from our `Logger` because `Log` covers them.

`testlog` now honours the context; its `SetContext` used to be a no-op. So records from devtest and acceptance-test loggers now carry `scope=…` (and `chainID=…` where set), and context-based logfilter rules apply to them. The set of shown and muted lines doesn't change, because the only rule installed in-tree filters by level.

Our `With`/`New` return our `Logger`, so it can't satisfy geth's `log.Logger` directly, because Go has no covariant return types. `ToGeth` converts a logger for the one go-ethereum API that takes one (discv5 in op-node). `SetDefault` also installs our logger as geth's global logger, so geth code running in-process logs through it. Returning geth's `log.Logger` from `With` instead would break 200+ call sites against upstream. The geth view keeps geth's `Write` semantics so that geth's own `log.Info` still attributes records to the geth call site. Handlers and level helpers stay re-exported from go-ethereum, since they exist upstream. `geth.go` is the only file allowed to import it.

Note: logfilter's `TestThreadSafety` races under `-race` because `testlog.CapturingHandler` has no lock. This is pre-existing, reproduces without this PR, and will be fixed in a follow-up.

Stacked on #23017. Part of #22752.
